title: Unified Inference: Product PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (v30)
author: Aisha Navarro
body:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates the product-level requirements, high-level design, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging notes, and the release plan for Unified Inference v30 (internal codename: Polaris). It is intended for product, engineering, go-to-market, and support teams.

Short summary: v30 focuses on (1) reducing tail latency for multi-tenant hosted customers via adaptive routing and predictive batching, (2) improving Dedicated autoscaling efficiency for long-tail workloads, (3) introducing a simplified pricing tier for hybrid Private/Dedicated customers, and (4) rolling out a telemetry-first quality monitoring pipeline tied to prompt-based evals.

Goals (top-level)
-----------------
- Improve 95th and 99th percentile generation latency for text & chat endpoints by 20–30% for common models.
- Reduce per-token cost for typical PLG workloads (short-text generation, summarization) by 15% through smarter batching and caching.
- Provide a simple hybrid pricing offering (Hosted+Dedicated burst) for mid-market customers.
- Ship telemetry-driven quality monitoring with automatic regression alerting tied to saved prompt sets.

Stakeholders and ownership
-------------------------
- Product lead: Aisha Navarro
- Eng owners: Mateo Ruiz (serving runtime), Daniel Kim (platform & routing), Priya Shah (billing & pricing)
- SRE / Reliability: SLO owners in eng-sre team (contact: Jordan Li)
- Go-to-market & Pricing: Marissa Cole
- Customer Success: Ravi Patel

Personas
--------
1. ML Engineers at startups (fast time-to-value; care about latency/cost tradeoffs).
2. Platform/Infra teams at mid-market/enterprise (need predictability, SLAs, private deployment).
3. Product Engineers building chat/assistant features (care about quality and predictable latency).

Success metrics (OKRs for v30 release window)
-------------------------------------------
- Product: 10% increase in DAU of teams using polling/streaming endpoints by Q2 post-release.
- Performance: 20% drop in 95p latency for hosted small-medium models measured on standard workload harness.
- Cost: 15% reduction in per-token unit cost (measured on cohort of PLG customers).
- Reliability: Maintain 99.95% availability for hosted API; Dedicated customers maintain contract SLAs.

PRD: Requirements and Acceptance Criteria
----------------------------------------
Intro: The PRD below lists functional and non-functional requirements. Each requirement includes an acceptance criteria and owner.

Requirements table (columns: id | requirement | priority | acceptance_criteria | owner)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- RQ-001 | Adaptive model routing by latency/cost policy | high | Policy can route 99% of requests within SLO tiers and fallback within 3s for cannot-serve cases; tests: synthetic routing failure & fallback | owner: Daniel Kim
- RQ-002 | Predictive batching engine (inference-window aware) | high | End-to-end perf tests show 15% lower per-token cost on typical PLG workload; must expose tunable batch-size and latency cap | owner: Mateo Ruiz
- RQ-003 | KV/prefix cache extension across requests for conversational flows | medium | 10% token savings on conversational workloads in perf harness; cache invalidation documented | owner: Mateo Ruiz
- RQ-004 | Dedicated autoscaling policy improvements (long-tail utilization smoothing) | high | Reduce peak cold-starts by 40% under synthetic traffic spikes; autoscaling policy documented and tested | owner: Eng-sre + Eng-platform
- RQ-005 | Pricing: Hybrid Hosted+Dedicated tier for mid-market customers | high | Clear pricing document and billing integration; offer includes committed base + hosted burst at defined rates | owner: Priya Shah
- RQ-006 | Telemetry-driven quality monitoring for saved prompt sets (evaluations + regression alerts) | high | UI shows evaluation trends, alerting threshold configurable; alerts triggered on statistically significant quality regressions | owner: Applied ML & Evals
- RQ-007 | Backwards-compatible API changes; maintain existing client SDKs | critical | No breaking changes; all public endpoints pass integration tests across SDKs | owner: Eng-devexp
- RQ-008 | Security & compliance checklist for Private deployments | medium | KMS/HSM integration validated; audit log format certified by security team | owner: Security & Compliance

Non-functional requirements
---------------------------
- SLOs: 99.95% availability for Hosted API; 95th p latency targets per model class (see SLO matrix below).
- Observability: per-request tracing, token-level cost attribution, and per-model route dashboards.
- Backups: model config & rollout metadata persisted in durable store with 30-day retention.

SLO matrix (model classes)
-------------------------
- small-text (<= 2k tokens): p95 < 150ms, p99 < 450ms
- medium-text (2k-8k tokens): p95 < 300ms, p99 < 900ms
- long-context (>8k tokens): p95 < 800ms, p99 < 2400ms
Availability: Hosted API >= 99.95% monthly.

Design Spec (high-level)
------------------------
Architecture summary:
- Serving runtime: existing GPU-optimized inference engine (service: redwood-runtime) with new predictive-batcher plugin and adaptive-router.
- Control plane: redwood-control manages model catalog, rollout metadata, and routing policies.
- Observability pipeline: events -> kafka -> evals-service (applied-ml) + metrics -> prometheus -> grafana dashboards; traces -> jaeger.

Key components and changes:
1) Adaptive Router (redwood-router):
   - Decision inputs: model profile, region, SLO tier, current queue depth, historical cold-start signal.
   - Policies: latency-first, cost-first, hybrid.
   - Fallbacks: automatic model-variant fallback (quantized variant) if selected node cannot serve within configured fallback_time_ms (default 3000ms).

2) Predictive Batcher (runtime plugin):
   - Uses short-term traffic forecasting (exponential smoothing) per route to pre-allocate batch windows.
   - Parameters exposed: target_latency_ms (default 50ms), max_batch_size (default 64), warmup_threshold.
   - Implementation notes: leverages continuous batching path; avoids blocking high-priority low-latency requests.

3) Telemetry-first quality monitoring:
   - Eval sets stored per-customer; periodic offline evals and streaming evaluation hooks for sampling production responses.
   - Alerts: configurable thresholds (absolute and relative regression).

4) Billing integration (pricing engine):
   - Pricing constructs: hosted base usage (per-token), dedicated committed capacity (monthly commit), hybrid burst multipliers.
   - Billing events include: token_count, model_id, route_id, customer_tier, commit_usage_applied.

API and SDK changes
-------------------
- New fields on /v1/generate: routing_policy (optional), prompt_set_id (optional, for telemetry).
- New admin API: /v1/admin/routing-policies (CRUD) guarded by admin role.
- SDKs: v3.5.0 releases include helpers for prompt_set bindings and automatic instrumentation.
- Backwards compatibility: routing_policy optional; default behavior preserved.

Design diagrams (text)
----------------------
- Sequence: Client -> API Gateway -> redwood-router -> redwood-runtime (predictive-batcher -> model worker) -> cache (KV) -> response.
- Dataflow: Production responses -> trace + eval-sampler -> kafka -> evals-service + metrics store.

Security considerations
-----------------------
- Private deployment mode: ensure routing decision data does not leave customer VPC. The router can run in control-plane or customer-managed sidecar depending on deployment.
- Audit logs: include routing decisions, model variant used, and fallback events.

Roadmap and Themes (Q1–Q3 next 3 quarters)
-------------------------------------------
- Q1 (stabilize & pilot):
  - Complete runtime plugin and router PoC; run internal perf benchmark suite; pilot with 3 enterprise customers on Dedicated.
  - Deliver pricing draft and legal approved contract terms for hybrid offering.
- Q2 (widen rollout & GTM enablement):
  - Enable telemetry pipeline and UI in Redwood Console (basic eval dashboards).
  - Publish customer-facing pricing page and sales playbook; launch beta for hybrid tier.
- Q3 (scale & optimize):
  - Full hosted rollout with gradual traffic migration; optimize autoscaling policies and cost heuristics.
  - SDKs and quickstarts published; case study with pilot customer.

Milestones and dates (target)
----------------------------
- 2028-11-15: Complete design & PRD (this doc).
- 2028-12-20: Runtime & router PoC complete; internal perf results.
- 2029-02-15: Pilot customers onboarded (Dedicated + hybrid).
- 2029-04-01: Beta public release (select customers).
- 2029-06-15: GA release (v30).

Pricing and Packaging Notes
-------------------------
Rationale: mid-market customers need predictability but keep cloud flexibility. Hybrid tier offers committed baseline (Dedicated) plus hosted burst credits. Pricing aligns with cost improvements from batching/caching and value delivered by telemetry.

Proposed tiers (high level):
- Pay-as-you-go (Hosted): per-token generation & embedding rates unchanged for v30 baseline.
- Committed Dedicated (Reserved): monthly GPU pool commit priced by vCPU/GPU-hour equivalent with tiered discounts (3-month / 12-month).
- Hybrid Hosted+Dedicated (New):
  - Base: monthly commit (e.g., 1x 8-GPU equivalent) at Dedicated rate.
  - Burst: hosted pool usage billed at burst_rate = hosted_rate * 1.5 (discounted if over commit threshold).
  - Feature add-ons: premium observability retention (+30 days), enhanced SLAs, evals-suite.

Billing examples (illustrative)
-----------------------------
- Customer A: 8-GPU commit at $X/month + 100M tokens hosted burst at $0.0009/token (burst multiplier applied).
- Customer B (PLG): stays on Hosted only; cost decreased in practice due to predictive batching savings (expected ~15% lower bill on comparable usage).

Packaging and Sales Playbook bullets
----------------------------------
- For customers with predictable baseline traffic > 2M tokens/day recommend Hybrid tier.
- For bursty customers with security requirements recommend Dedicated + Private deployment.
- Offer a 90-day pilot discount for early adopters (sales-approved).

Release Notes (v30 alpha -> beta -> GA)
--------------------------------------
v30.0-alpha (internal, 2028-12-20)
- New: adaptive-router prototype and predictive-batcher plugin (internal flag).
- Telemetry: eval-sampling hook added to runtime.
- Known issues: caching warmed only after 10k requests; dev teams to monitor.

v30.0-beta (pilot, 2029-02-15)
- New: admin routing policies UI, prompt_set binding in API, console eval dashboard (beta).
- Improved: Dedicated autoscaling tunables and policies.
- Breaking changes: none.
- Migration notes: No client-side changes required; enable new features via admin console.

v30.0 (GA, 2029-06-15 target)
- New: Hybrid pricing published; SDK v3.5.0 GA; telemetry alerts integrated in Console; default routing_policy: hybrid.
- Performance: expected 20% p95 latency improvement on small/medium model classes (measured internally).
- Rollout plan: staged migration for hosted traffic (see rollout checklist).

Rollout checklist (owners & steps)
---------------------------------
1. Engineering (serving runtime)
   - [ ] Merge predictive-batcher into main and enable feature-flag gating.
   - [ ] Perf test against benchmark harness; publish results to dashboards.
2. Platform & Router
   - [ ] Deploy redwood-router to canary region (us-west-2) with routing_policy=latency-first.
   - [ ] Smoke tests for fallback behavior and audit logging.
3. Billing & Pricing
   - [ ] Publish pricing page; integrate hybrid pricing into billing engine.
   - [ ] Test billing events for hybrid consumption in sandbox.
4. Console & Observability
   - [ ] Ship eval dashboards and alerting; configure default thresholds for pilot customers.
5. Customer Success & Sales
   - [ ] Onboard pilot customers; run 2-week pilot and collect feedback.
6. Security & Compliance
   - [ ] Validate Private deployment checklist and KMS integration.

Rollback plan
-------------
- If p95 latency or error rates regress beyond tolerance (defined as +20% over baseline or availability < 99.9%), automatically disable adaptive-router and fall back to previous routing logic. Engineers must revert feature-flag within 30 minutes and open incident.

Open risks and mitigations
-------------------------
- Risk: Predictive batching increases tail latency for rare small requests.
  - Mitigation: Low-latency requests bypass large-batch paths; batcher respects per-route latency caps.
- Risk: Pricing complexity confuses customers.
  - Mitigation: Provide worked examples, sales playbook, and a pricing calculator in Console.
- Risk: Telemetry data volume and privacy for Private customers.
  - Mitigation: Telemetry sampling, PII filtering, and customer opt-out for Private + dedicated-only mode.

Appendix
--------
- CLI example: bind a prompt set to a route (YAML snippet)

  $ redwood route create --name "assistant-chat" --model "rw-4b" --prompt-set-id "ps-1234" --routing-policy "hybrid"

- Example API generate payload (JSON)
  {
    "model": "rw-4o",
    "input": "Summarize the following doc...",
    "routing_policy": "latency-first",
    "prompt_set_id": "ps-1234"
  }

- Perf benchmark command (internal harness)

  $ scripts/run_bench --model rw-4b --profile plg-short --concurrency 200 --duration 10m

Contact and next steps
----------------------

- Runtime & routing design questions: Mateo Ruiz (eng-serving-runtime), Daniel Kim (eng-platform).
- Pricing and billing: Priya Shah (finance-product).

Please review and add comments directly on this page. The next review checkpoint is 2028-11-22 (roadmap grooming meeting).
